title: Weighted Range-Constrained Ising-Model Decoder for Quantum Error Correction
problem: Quantum error correction decoders must balance time complexity and error detection threshold; existing Ising-model decoders have higher complexity than union-find but inferior threshold compared to minimum-weight perfect-matching (MWPM).
motivation: Scalable quantum error correction is essential for practical quantum computing, but decoder efficiency and fidelity are bottlenecks; Ising-based approaches offer structural advantages but need optimization.
method: The decoder uses a polygon to enclose the locations where errors were detected (called flipped syndromes), guaranteeing coverage of all possible error chains. Within this geometric boundary, it tunes the Ising model's parameters—the coupling strengths (how variables interact) and field coefficients (external biases)—through constraint-based optimization to find settings that preserve error-detection accuracy while keeping calculations manageable.
key_novelty: A geometric constraint (a polygon) around error locations reduces the Ising model variables by 97.8x, enabling O(n) worst-case runtime that beats union-find and achieving a 10.71-11.0% error threshold superior to MWPM.
contributions: Weighted Range-Constrained Ising formulation reducing variable count by 97.8x
Microsecond-level decoding achieving O(n) worst-case time complexity outperforming union-find
Threshold up to 10.71-11.0% surpassing reported MWPM performance
limitations: Practical quantum hardware implementation and scalability to larger error correction codes not discussed.
primary_theme: Optimized Ising decoder for quantum error correction
